subject: Residency control & snapshot handover playbook
messages:
From: Adam Liu <adam.liu@medtech.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Residency control: snapshot handover & proof of deletion

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our compliance team has one tight ask before we sign: a concrete, auditable playbook for handing over periodic storage snapshots from Redwood Private (VPC) to our environment and an end-to-end timeline and proof of deletion when we request tenant wipe. They want to understand who has custody at each step, retention windows for intermediate artifacts, and the attestation artifacts we can expect.

High-level questions to start:
- Can snapshots be created and transferred entirely within our VPC boundary (customer-owned storage)?
- If not, what minimal metadata leaves Redwood systems and how is it protected?
- When we request a tenant deletion, what evidence (hashes, signed statements, logs) do you provide and how quickly?

Attached is our questionnaire (medtech_data_residency_questions.xlsx) with some specifics. Could you propose a playbook and a timeline we can take to our security reviewers?

Appreciate a concise response. We’re trying to close by end of the month.

Thanks,
Adam Liu\Director of IT Security\MedTech Solutions
[attachment: medtech_data_residency_questions.xlsx]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Adam Liu <adam.liu@medtech.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency control: snapshot handover & proof of deletion

Hi Adam — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. Looping in Marissa (Customer Success — onboarding) and Ben (Prod Security) so we can provide both the operational playbook and the attestation artifacts you’ll need.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Yes — for Redwood Private deployed into customer-managed object storage (S3-compatible), snapshots can be created, encrypted, and written directly to your storage bucket so data never leaves your tenancy.
- When snapshots are transferred, Redwood only records immutable metadata pointers (snapshot ID, object keys, size, creation timestamp, and SHA256 checksums). Those metadata records are stored in our control plane for operational tracing and are encrypted at rest.
- Deletion: when you request tenant wipe, we execute a multi-step erase and provide: signed deletion manifest (timestamped), checksum verification for removed objects, and a redwood-execution-trace (audit log excerpt) showing erase progression. Typical turnaround: 48–72 hours for evidence package on standard requests; expedited options available.

Proposed snapshot handover playbook (high level):
1) Prep (Day 0): Customer provides target bucket ARN, KMS key ID (customer-managed ideally), and a small test object for access verification.
2) Snapshot creation (Day 1): In-tenant snapshot is created; blocks are deduplicated client-side where possible and encrypted with the provided KMS key. Snapshot manifest (includes SHA256 checksums per object) is generated.
3) Upload (Day 1–2): Snapshot objects are uploaded directly to the customer bucket using presigned URLs scoped to the upload window; no snapshot data flows through Redwood-hosted object storage.
4) Verification (Day 2): Redwood and MedTech run a verification step — Redwood returns manifest and signatures so your security team can validate checksums.
5) Handover confirmation (Day 2): Signed confirmation email + Drive link to manifest and a PDF attestation (attached: redwood_snapshot_handover_v1.pdf).
6) Retention & deletion (on demand): Customer issues tenant-wipe via console or support ticket. Redwood performs: logical unlink -> S3 object deletion -> overwrite/retire intermediate caches -> provide signed deletion manifest and audit excerpt.

Notes on evidence and non-repudiation:
- Signed manifests: We sign manifests with our platform key and timestamp; you can validate signatures against our published verification key.
- Audit excerpts: Provide a sequence of operation logs (operation ids and timestamps) that map to the manifest. For high-sensitivity accounts we support a notarized HSM-backed timestamp on request (extra-miles offering).
- Escrow: If you’d like an additional custody control, we can support dual-writes to an escrow bucket (customer-managed) with delegated read-only keys for your auditors.

Attachments: redwood_snapshot_handover_v1.pdf (playbook + sample manifest). Also pushed a copy of the manifest template into the Drive folder (see link below).

Can you confirm: preferred KMS approach (customer-managed vs. Redwood-managed), and whether you need the notarized HSM timestamps? Once we have that I’ll surface a concise checklist for your procurement and security teams.

Best,
Tessa Morgan\Enterprise Solutions\Redwood Inference

From: Adam Liu <adam.liu@medtech.io>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency control: snapshot handover & proof of deletion

Thanks, Tessa — this is very helpful. Quick clarifying questions from our compliance reviewer:
1) "Presigned URL" uploads are acceptable, but can you confirm the upload endpoints are restricted to our bucket and that the URL window is short-lived?
2) For the signed manifests: can Redwood provide both the signed manifest and the raw manifest (unsigned) so we can independently run the checksum verification flow?
3) On deletion: what guarantees do you provide around intermediate KV cache and backups created by the runtime (not S3 objects) — are those ephemeral in our VPC and removed on wipe?

If you can answer those three items and affirm the 48–72 hour evidence timeline, we can move to procurement.

On KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys if possible. Also — the notarized HSM timestamp is something we might request for our more regulated flows; please include pricing delta if that’s not standard.

—Adam

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Adam’s questions and my proposed playbook. Answers to Adam’s items below so we can align on the reply + procurement checklist:

1) Presigned URL scope / window: yes — URLs are scoped to the target bucket/prefix and expire by default in 15 minutes. We can tighten to a single-use upload token if requested (small ops change).
2) Signed + raw manifest: we’ll deliver both. The raw manifest is the authoritative list of objects and checksums; redwood signs the manifest and retains a copy in encrypted control-plane logs for a rolling 90-day audit window (we can extend per contract).
3) Runtime intermediate state: all KV caches are memory-resident in the deployed runtime and any persisted checkpoints are written into the customer bucket when configured. During tenant-wipe we execute a runtime GC and provide an audit log showing GC completion. For extra assurance we can run a checksum mismatch scan to show objects referenced by the runtime are no longer present.

Next actions I propose:
- Marissa: assemble procurement checklist (bucket + KMS info, contact for auditing, required Drive access).
- Ben: prepare a short security attestation template (we can include HSM timestamp pricing if you confirm it's needed).
- I’ll draft the short customer-facing playbook and the one-page evidence checklist.

Ben — can you confirm the HSM notarization incremental cost (rough ballpark) so we can include it in the reply?

Thanks — I’ll aim to send the customer-facing reply by EOD after internal signoff.

Best,
Tessa Morgan\Enterprise Solutions\Redwood Inference
